investigation.title: Remote Agent Pod Scheduling Failure: Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity Across All Available Nodes
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-18T08:55–09:02Z because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence was collected (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing), confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource (peer-pod VM slots) had no remaining allocatable capacity, and four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-constrained nodes. Because the pod never became schedulable within the eval's timeout window (~144–146 s), the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the remote-agent-create contract (vmIdPresent, remoteState, orgId, agentId). This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no evidence of a user-traffic or broader service outage is present in the supplied packet.

possibleCauses: Primary — kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource exhausted on the 2 eligible nodes: all peer-pod VM slots on the only nodes that match the pod's affinity/selector are currently allocated to other workloads, leaving no room for new remote-agent pods. This is directly stated in the scheduler message (evidence: failed-check.message).

Secondary — node affinity or node selector misconfiguration: the pod's scheduling constraints restrict it to a subset of nodes (only 2 of 6 qualify for the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource), making the cluster effectively smaller than its nominal 6-node size for remote-agent workloads. If the affinity rules are overly restrictive or stale, eligible node count could be lower than intended.

Tertiary — cluster capacity not scaled to meet concurrent eval demand: all three sibling checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) ran near-simultaneously and each required a peer-pod VM slot. If the 2 eligible nodes have a small VM slot quota, concurrent eval runs could exhaust capacity quickly.
Lower confidence — a transient spike in other workloads consuming kata.peerpods.io/vm slots on the 2 eligible nodes at the time of the eval run, causing temporary exhaustion that may self-resolve.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Pods Unschedulable Due to Exhausted kata.peerpods.io/vm Capacity — All Three Remote-Agent Checks Failing
investigation.summary: All three remote-agent eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-18T08:57–09:02Z with an identical Kubernetes scheduling error: the cluster's 6 nodes could not schedule the requested peer-pod because only 2 nodes carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource and both are already at capacity, while the remaining 4 nodes do not match the pod's node affinity/selector. Because the agent pod never started, the eval runner's createAgent call never returned a live agent, so no evidence (orgId, agentId, readyState, state) was ever written and the expected-output contract was fully violated.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes cluster backing the remote-agent swarm has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm resource on the 2 eligible nodes. When the eval runner called createAgent for a "remote" agent (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs line 1905), the resulting pod was left Unschedulable for ~142–146 seconds across all three checks before the eval timed out. No agent was ever provisioned, so the probe could not collect orgId, agentId, readyState, or state, causing a complete contract gap. This is a Kubernetes infrastructure capacity constraint, not an application code defect, and is localized to the remote-agent scheduling path in the production-api environment. No user-traffic or incident signals are present in the supplied evidence; this is an eval-layer failure reflecting an infrastructure condition.

Preemption was attempted and found no victims, ruling out a simple priority fix.

[Medium confidence] Node affinity/selector mismatch on 4 of 6 nodes: the remote-agent pod spec requires a node label or taint that only 2 nodes satisfy. If those 2 nodes are also at VM capacity, any new remote-agent pod will always be Unschedulable regardless of overall cluster load.

[Lower confidence] Node pool scaling policy not triggering: the cluster autoscaler may not be configured to add kata.peerpods.io/vm-capable nodes in response to pending pods, leaving the resource gap unresolved.

investigation.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed on 2026-07-18 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message indicating that the 6-node production cluster has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod VM capacity on the 2 eligible nodes, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) entirely absent.
investigation.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place remote-agent pods because the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource report Insufficient capacity, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion or misconfiguration in the production-api cluster, not an application code defect. The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1918: createAgent with type "remote") depends on a successfully scheduled peer-pod VM to produce any evidence; with scheduling blocked, the probe times out and returns no evidence, causing the expected-output contract for orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message to be entirely unmet.

Tertiary — peer-pod VM quota set too low for the cluster size: the kata.peerpods.io/vm resource limit on the 2 eligible nodes may be under-provisioned relative to concurrent eval and production workload demand.

Quaternary — leaked or zombie remote-agent pods from prior eval runs holding VM slots without being cleaned up, preventing new pods from scheduling (the withCleanup wrapper in run-status-probes.mjs is intended to prevent this, but a prior crash or timeout could leave residual pods).

investigations.summary: All three remote-agents checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed in production-api at 2026-07-18T08:55–09:02Z because every pod submitted to the Kubernetes cluster was rejected as Unschedulable: the 2 nodes carrying the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource reported insufficient capacity, and the remaining 4 nodes did not match the pod's node affinity or selector. No evidence was collected (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState all missing), confirming the agent VM was never provisioned.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler could not place the remote-agent pod on any of the 6 available nodes. Two nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource (peer-pod VM slots) had no remaining allocatable capacity, and four nodes were excluded by the pod's node affinity or node selector. Preemption was also unavailable on both resource-constrained nodes. Because the pod never became schedulable within the eval's timeout window (~144–146 s), the agent VM was never created, and the eval runner received no evidence to satisfy the remote-agent-create contract (vmIdPresent, remoteState, orgId, agentId). This is an infrastructure-layer scheduling failure localized to the remote-agents feature in the production-api environment; no evidence of a user-traffic or broader service outage is present in the supplied packet.

investigations.title: Remote Agent Eval Failure: Kubernetes kata.peerpods.io/vm Resource Exhaustion Blocking Pod Scheduling
investigations.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed on 2026-07-18 with an identical Kubernetes scheduler message indicating that the 6-node production cluster has exhausted its kata.peerpods.io/vm peer-pod VM capacity on the 2 eligible nodes, and the remaining 4 nodes do not satisfy the pod's node affinity or selector constraints. Because no remote agent pod could be scheduled, the eval runner's createAgent call never completed, leaving all required evidence fields (orgId, agentId, model, provider, message) entirely absent.
investigations.rootCause: The Kubernetes scheduler cannot place remote-agent pods because the 2 nodes that carry the kata.peerpods.io/vm extended resource report Insufficient capacity, and the other 4 nodes are excluded by the pod's node affinity/selector rules. This is an infrastructure-layer resource exhaustion or misconfiguration in the production-api cluster, not an application code defect. The eval runner (infra/evals/status/run-status-probes.mjs, line 1918: createAgent with type "remote") depends on a successfully scheduled peer-pod VM to produce any evidence; with scheduling blocked, the probe times out and returns no evidence, causing the expected-output contract for orgId, agentId, model, provider, and message to be entirely unmet.
